page: Microsoft Azure E112iads_v5 is an isolated virtual machine instance from the EIADSv5 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 112 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 56 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 3891 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10%. Single-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests. Memory performance is split, with small-block cached read-only bandwidth reaching top-tier levels, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths remain in the average tier. Cryptographic operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a top-tier PassMark CPU encryption score. Database operations and Redis SET operations both register strong performance in the top 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E112iads_v5 offers high resource density, combining massive compute capacity with substantial memory and local storage. This makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database hosting, and data-heavy enterprise applications. The lack of GPU acceleration makes it less suitable for heavy deep learning training, but its strong CPU performance supports efficient medium-sized LLM inference prompt processing. It is recommended for relational databases, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
